correctness.rationale: All n>=2 and 0<=k<=n^2: exact mixed-row/column degree-one event count splits on their shared edge, yielding P and J and n^2(J-P^2). Cancellation yields the finite product identity for k=Theta(n). Taylor expansions are uniform for k/n in a compact positive range; the O(n^-4) remainder uses j=O(n) and O(n) terms. Fixed-c and critical-window asymptotics follow. Independently enumerated all 2x2 through 4x4 binary matrices and checked 1302 exact assertions. Critical boundary x=+-2/sqrt(3) and finite all-k sign pattern not asserted.

originality.rationale: Best-knowledge new combination: exact fixed-edge two-sided unary-degree covariance and a nontrivial square-root critical window with a sign reversal at |x|=2/sqrt(3). McKay--Skerman analyzes the model but Theorem 1(c) explicitly excludes sparse p=Theta(1/n), while its surrogate has zero cross-part covariance. Earlier degree-count sources remain an acknowledged priority risk, not proof of coverage.

No proof of uniqueness or universal originality follows from semantic searches or partition-specific publication results.

value.rationale: Opposite-side degree-one counts are interpretable as counts of dangling vertices in a two-type network, central for local coverage/connectivity. Conditioning the total edge count couples the two sides in competing ways. The leading negative covariance cancels at the natural mean-degree threshold two and reveals a genuinely narrower O(sqrt(n)) positive-covariance window, an interpretable dependence reversal not apparent from marginal laws or dense degree-sequence approximations. The complete exact formula is also useful for finite fixed-edge inference.
